provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Reports a condition actually met: a plain non-past clause names an event that did happen, and the past main clause tells what the speaker then found or what followed on its heels (角を曲がると海が見えた). The sibling と states a hypothetical or habitual rule with a non-past main clause (春が来ると桜が咲く); the particle lanes list nouns (パンと卵) or name a companion (友達と話す). A command, request or intention normally cannot follow it; use たら.

examples.ruby: 窓[まど]を開[あ]けると冷[つめ]たい風[かぜ]が入[はい]ってきた。
examples.english: The moment I opened the window, a cold draft blew in.

examples.ruby: 玄関[げんかん]を出[で]ると、隣[となり]の猫[ねこ]が座[すわ]っていた。
examples.english: When I stepped out the front door, the neighbor's cat was sitting there.

examples.ruby: 祖母[そぼ]は私[わたし]の顔[かお]を見[み]ると、急[きゅう]に泣[な]き出[だ]した。
examples.english: The moment my grandmother saw my face, she burst into tears.

patterns.usage_note: Takes a premise that has just been established or claimed, treats it as fact, and states the conclusion the speaker draws from it: 彼の話が本当だとすると、計画は来月から変わる. The sibling lane is the same string floating a supposition the speaker is only entertaining and asking what would follow (仮に会場を変えるとすれば). It follows the plain form, past included (彼が犯人だったとすると), with だ after a noun; the polite form is としますと.

examples.ruby: 熱[ねつ]が本当[ほんとう]に三十九度[さんじゅうきゅうど]だとすると、今日[きょう]は休[やす]むしかない。
examples.english: If the fever really is thirty-nine degrees, there's nothing for it but to stay home today.

examples.ruby: 彼[かれ]の話[はなし]が本当[ほんとう]だとすると、計画[けいかく]は来月[らいげつ]から変[か]わる。
examples.english: If what he says is true, then the plan changes starting next month.

examples.ruby: レシピの砂糖[さとう]が大[おお]さじ三[さん]だとすると、ちょっと甘[あま]すぎる。
examples.english: If the recipe really calls for three tablespoons of sugar, that's a bit too sweet.

glosses: with … like this; as things stand
patterns.usage_note: Takes the situation actually in front of the speaker as grounds for a negative conclusion, typically pointing at it with こう or この: この雨じゃ, こう暑くちゃ, 給料がこれじゃ. The sibling senses are a merely supposed condition, 六時じゃ, and a warning about an action someone performs, 飲んじゃ. Because the consequent is an assessment that something will not work out, requests and invitations rarely follow.

examples.ruby: この雨[あめ]じゃ花火[はなび]大会[たいかい]は中止[ちゅうし]だろうね。
examples.english: With rain like this, the fireworks are bound to be called off.

examples.ruby: こう暑[あつ]くちゃ何[なに]もする気[き]になれない。
examples.english: When it's this hot, you can't work up the will to do anything.

examples.ruby: 給料[きゅうりょう]がこれじゃ都会[とかい]で暮[く]らしていけないよ。
examples.english: On a salary like this, there's no way to keep living in the city.

patterns.usage_note: The all-purpose ta-stem conditional: it sets up one concrete occasion and says what holds once it comes about (駅に着いたら電話して, 高かったらやめる). A sibling entry is the clipped sentence-final たら that suggests a course of action to the listener, 少し休んだら. だら is this same form after verbs whose plain past voices, 読んだら, 泳いだら, and unlike と the main clause may be a request, command, or the speaker's own intention.

examples.ruby: 駅[えき]に着[つ]いたら電話[でんわ]してください。
examples.english: Give me a call once you get to the station.

examples.ruby: この本[ほん]を読[よ]んだら妹[いもうと]に貸[か]すつもりだ。
examples.english: Once I finish this book, I plan to lend it to my little sister.

examples.ruby: 家[いえ]に帰[かえ]ったら玄関[げんかん]の鍵[かぎ]が開[あ]いていた。
examples.english: When I got home, the front door was unlocked.

glosses: when you try …, it turns out …
patterns.usage_note: Marks the preceding action as the occasion of a discovery: the main clause reports what came to light, usually in the past and usually something the speaker did not expect (調べてみると古い手紙が出てきた). で appears wherever the て-form is voiced (読んでみると, 泳いでみると), て elsewhere. てみたら is interchangeable here, but てみれば reads as reflective or hypothetical (考えてみれば), and 振り返ってみると and 考えてみると keep みると.

examples.ruby: 棚[たな]の奥[おく]を調[しら]べてみると古[ふる]い手紙[てがみ]が出[で]てきた。
examples.english: When I dug around at the back of the shelf, an old letter turned up.

examples.ruby: その本[ほん]を読[よ]んでみると意外[いがい]に面白[おもしろ]かった。
examples.english: I gave the book a try, and it was unexpectedly good.

examples.ruby: 実際[じっさい]に計算[けいさん]してみると予想[よそう]より費用[ひよう]がかかった。
examples.english: Once I actually ran the numbers, it came to more than I'd figured.
